name: Basilica and National Shrine of Our Lady of Lebanon
history: Maronite priests first proposed a U.S. shrine to Our Lady of Lebanon in 1960. Maronites of the Youngstown area took it up; land was bought in 1961 and the shrine established in 1963. Ground was broken in August 1964 and the shrine was dedicated on 15 August 1965. Pope Francis named it a basilica in 2014.
arch: A replica of the shrine at Harissa, Lebanon: a tall tower carrying a statue of the Virgin Mary beside the church.
features: It is a basilica of the Maronite Catholic Church, an Eastern Catholic church of Lebanese origin.
The whole facility was completed for $200,000.

look.d: As at Harissa, Mary stands atop a tower with open arms.
The statue was placed on the tower before the dedication in 1965.

fun: It is one of the few U.S. basilicas of an Eastern Catholic church.
journal: A piece of Lebanon in the Ohio fields. Mary on her tower, arms wide.
